title: When the Veil Sings Again
premise: Wendell Lockridge has spent her life as a bone-carver in the border town of Thornfell, listening to the dead smuggled through the mountains and telling no one what she hears. When a scholar arrives carrying a century-old book of prophecies that names her—and tonight's date—as the night the vanished kingdom of Vael opens its last door, Wendell is dragged into a hunt led by the Crown's Inquisitor, who believes the door must be sealed forever. Guided by the ghosts she has always heard and a ragtag found family of smugglers, deserters, and one very stubborn prophet's descendant, Wendell learns the dead of Vael are not haunting the mountains but waiting to go home. At the climax she must choose between sealing the door to save her friends' lives or opening it and letting truth destroy her country's founding lie; she opens it, the dead pass through, and Wendell—no longer invisible—stays behind to carve their names into living stone.
about_author: Ulyana Pemberton is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town folklore before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted chapel in the northern hills, where she insists the acoustics are 'conducive to hearing things.'

chapters.title: The Carver's Quiet Hours
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She finishes a memorial bone-carving for a drowned smuggler while privately hearing his ghost complain about the wrong river being named on it. Establishes her gift, her isolation, and her rule: never repeat what the dead say aloud. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as discipline.

chapters.title: A Stranger with a Borrowed Book
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Scholar Ilsa Verrow arrives seeking passage through Thornfell, carrying a prophecy book written a century ago. Wendell glimpses her own name and tonight's date on its page and lies about it. Emotional beat: the first crack in her invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember of Vael
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa explains the vanished kingdom: erased from maps after a royal massacre, its survivors scattered, its records burned. The prophecy says the last door reopens once, for one night, when 'the carver who hears' stands before it. Emotional beat: dread disguised as academic curiosity.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor Comes at Dusk
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Corvane's POV. The Crown's agent reaches Thornfell hunting the prophecy book, executing a smuggler for information. He interviews Wendell and senses she is hiding something but lacks proof. Emotional beat: cold menace; the stakes become mortal.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Oath
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell recruits her found family—smuggler captain Bramble, deserter Hesk, and fence-girl Tally—to move Ilsa and the book over the mountains ahead of Corvane. Each joins for a private debt to the dead. Emotional beat: reluctant kinship forming.

chapters.title: The Road That Isn't on Any Map
chapters.summary: Hesk's POV. The company takes a ghost-road only Wendell can navigate by listening to dead travelers. A near-capture forces Tally to improvise a brilliant deception. Emotional beat: trust tested and earned under pressure.

chapters.title: Voices in the Pass
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The dead grow louder near the old border, whispering fragments of the massacre night. Wendell admits to Ilsa she has heard them since childhood and always pretended otherwise. Emotional beat: confession; loyalty vs. truth begins to sharpen.

chapters.title: Corvane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Flashback-tinged chapter revealing why he serves the seal: his ancestor helped erase Vael, and his family's honor rests on the lie staying buried. He closes the southern passes. Emotional beat: antagonist humanized without softened.

chapters.title: The Chapel of Unnamed Bones
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Sheltering in an ossuary chapel, the group finds bones of Vael's massacred court, unmarked for a century. Wendell reads their names from memory of their voices. Emotional beat: grief made communal; the dead become people.

chapters.title: Treachery at the Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Tally's POV. An old contact sells their route to Corvane. Ambush at the tollhouse; Hesk is gravely wounded covering the retreat. Emotional beat: betrayal's sting and the cost of loyalty.

chapters.title: The Prophet's Descendant
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa confesses she is descended from the prophet who wrote the book—and that her family has guarded a second half of the prophecy, hidden, which warns the door devours whoever opens it. Emotional beat: guilt and the weight of inheritance.

chapters.title: Where the Country Still Exists
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Crossing into land never formally ceded, the company finds living remnants of Vaeli culture—a shrine, a song, an old woman who recognizes Wendell's carving style as court-trained magic. Emotional beat: wonder; the past is not past.

chapters.title: Half a Prophecy
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. Deciphering the hidden half reveals two doors: one for the dead to leave, one for something else to enter if opened wrongly. The group fractures over whether to open anything at all. Emotional beat: found family's first real rupture.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane captures Tally and offers her freedom to betray the route. She gives him a true-but-useless path, buying time at terrible risk. Emotional beat: courage in small hands.

chapters.title: Night of the Thin Veil
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. They reach the door-site as the veil thins; the dead of Vael gather, visible now even to the others. Corvane's soldiers arrive simultaneously. Standoff begins. Emotional beat: awe colliding with terror.

chapters.title: What Corvane Cannot Burn
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa publicly reads the massacre record Corvane's family tried to destroy; his soldiers waver as the truth spreads through their ranks. Corvane orders the door sealed by force. Emotional beat: truth as weapon and wound.

chapters.title: The Door Devours
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. First attempt to open the door nearly kills Wendell—the hidden half was literal. She realizes the door demands a willing voice of both kingdoms: living and dead speaking together. Emotional beat: sacrifice made comprehensible.

chapters.title: Every Name, Spoken
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating brief POVs. The company and the dead recite the names of Vael together—Tally freed mid-battle, Hesk carried on a bier, even some of Corvane's soldiers joining. Emotional beat: unity forged from fracture.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Climax. The door opens fully only if someone stays to hold it from this side. Wendell volunteers; Corvane, broken by the truth, chooses instead to help her rather than seal it, redeeming nothing but choosing rightly at last. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved.

chapters.title: The Dead Go Home
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. The dead of Vael cross through singing; the mountains ring with the sound of a country remembering itself. The door closes gently behind them. Casualties are mourned; Hesk survives. Emotional beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Carved in Living Stone
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Resolution. Wendell remains in Thornfell, no longer hiding her gift, carving the recovered names into a public monument while the ghosts who remain choose to stay with her. Ilsa departs to rewrite the histories. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not stumbled into.

chapters.title: When the Veil Sings Again
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Wendell's POV. Years later, on the anniversary, the veil thins briefly and the door glows—not opening, just acknowledging. Wendell teaches an apprentice bone-carver to listen. Final line echoes the prophecy fulfilled differently than feared. Emotional beat: peace earned, story closed.
